thoughts.content: Confirmed: pod worker-7fdf4ffb67-n2mn9 in namespace shop is Pending (63s old), consistent with alert. Nodes are all Ready. Next: describe the pending pod for scheduling events, and check node resource capacity/allocation since this looks like a new ReplicaSet (worker-7fdf4ffb67) replacing an old one (worker-6cf88d4b58 still running) — possible rollout causing resource pressure.

Found strong evidence. The Pending pod requests cpu: 64 (64 whole CPU cores) — not 64 millicores. Compare: the sibling pod worker-6cf88d4b58-2l75l (old ReplicaSet, still Running) requests only 50m (0.05 CPU) per the node's allocated-resources table. Let me confirm this is a deployment spec issue by checking the Deployment object directly.

Investigation Summary

Alert: KubePodNotReady — pod worker-7fdf4ffb67-n2mn9 in namespace shop, Pending >5 min, cluster aurora-lab (kind-aurora-lab)

Findings (in order of investigation)

History check: No prior incidents for "shop" or this cluster in Aurora or memory — first occurrence, no stale pattern to disprove.

Confirmed symptom live: kubectl get pods -n shop shows worker-7fdf4ffb67-n2mn9 0/1 Ready / Pending, age 63-74s and growing (still Pending at time of writing).

Isolated failing component: kubectl describe pod worker-7fdf4ffb67-n2mn9 →
   ``
   PodScheduled: False
   Warning FailedScheduling: 0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 2 Insufficient cpu.
   preemption: 0/3 nodes are available: 3 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.
   `
   Pod requests: cpu: 64 (literal — 64 whole CPU cores, not 64m).

Ruled out node health: kubectl describe nodes — all 3 nodes Ready=True, no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure. Each worker node's Allocatable cpu is only 10 cores. The control-plane node carries the standard NoSchedule taint (expected, not new). So the "2 Insufficient cpu" is real: no node can ever satisfy a 64-core request — this is not transient resource contention, it is structurally impossible on this cluster.

Found the change: kubectl get deployment worker -n shop -o yaml (revision 2, generation 2) shows the live spec has resources.requests.cpu: "64", while the deployment's own kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation — i.e., the last correctly-applied/intended state — records requests.cpu: "50m". The live spec has drifted from the recorded desired state (someone ran kubectl edit/kubectl patch/kubectl set resources directly against the cluster, bypassing the normal apply flow, and set cpu to 64 instead of 64m/50m).

Corroborating evidence: The sibling pod from the previous (still-healthy) ReplicaSet worker-6cf88d4b58-2l75l is Running on worker2 with cpu request 50m (0%) — consistent with every other pod
